This document outlines 
the major maintenance procedures P1, to be performed every five years as 
indicated by Y5 in the title block.

This pump (4 pumps) function to wash 
the traveling water screens from plastics, wood, fungi, and greases.

The first draft is initiated by eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem, tested by eng. Zakria 
Radwan Hassanain, revised by eng. Samir Abdel Gelil: EDEPC 
inspection and quality control general director, accepted by eng. Mohamed Farag 
Anan: general manager, and approved by eng. Mohamed El-Sarrag: head sector of 
Damietta 3x135MW PS.

This document accepted by eng.
 Samir Abdel Gilel: EDEPC 
 inspection and 
 quality control general director & MPIS coordinator, and 
 certified by accountant: Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman EDEPC planning & financial 
 predicting head sector and supervisor of inspection & 
 quality control's head sector.

A work permit must be issued and the maintenance 
 staff should carry the suitable safety category.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Wear safety and healthy equipments as safety healthy, 
 safety shoes, ...etc.

A work permit must be issued and the maintenance 
 staff should carry the suitable safety category.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Wear safety and healthy equipments as safety healthy, 
 safety shoes, ...etc.
Isolate the CB of the pump motor.

Disconnect electric terminals of the pump 
 motor.

Isolate the pump mechanically by closing 
 suction and delivery valves.
Be sure that the pump is completely drained.
Complete maintenance tool set.
Cleaning fluid, Rags, soft brushes
Filler, vibrometer, Dial indicator.
Grease.

Check
 the vibration level of the pump and record it.

Check
 discharge, pressure and record them.
Check the alignment and record it.
Disconnect the motor.
Unbolt the coupling between the motor and the pump.
Remove the motor with its casing.
Dismantle every pipes connecting to the pump.
Remove the coupling key (10) and remove the coupling lower part.
Remove the water shield (32).
Remove the gland (241).
Remove the packing (11) and lantern (225).
Remove the upper shaft sleeve (233d).
Remove the casted discharged head (952).
Remove the flat gasket (3).
Unbolt the screws and the nuts (X1) to remove the top column (957).

Uncouple the coupling between the upper and intermediate shafts, remove the 
 coupling and raise the upper shaft.
Remove the guide bearing (( bushing (933) then the shaft sleeve (233c) )).
Unbolt the screws and the nuts (X2) to remove the lower column (926).

Uncouple the coupling between the intermediate and lower shafts, remove the 
 coupling and raise the intermediate shaft.
Unbolt the screws and the nuts (X3) to remove the discharge case (208).
Remove the bearing (234) then the shaft sleeve (233b).

Unbolt the screws and the nuts (X4) to remove the upper intermediate case 
 (209).
Remove the upper casing wear rings (223A) and impeller wear ring (224).

Unbolt the screws and the nuts (X5) to remove the lower intermediate case 
 (209).
Remove the upper casing wear rings (223) and impeller wear ring (224).
Raise the lower shaft with impeller.
Unbolt the cap (237).
Remove the stages of impeller and wear rings.
Now the pump is completely disassembled.
Clean all parts of the pump.
Change the bearings of the pump.
Check all parts for any worn-out, replace the damaged.
Check all parts for cracks, treat the cracks by grinding or remachining.
Inspect the run-out of the shafts.
Change the wearing rings.
Measure the radial clearances for the pump and adjust them.
Grease the bearings of the pump.
Clean all contact surfaces.
Assemble the lower casing wear ring.
Tight the cap (237) on the lower shaft.
Mount the key (9) on the shaft.
Assemble the first stage of impeller and fix it with the shaft by the key.

Mount the impeller first stage lower wear ring and reset the shaft with the 
 first stage on the suction casing.
Mount the impeller first stage upper wear ring.
Mount the shaft sleeves (233 & 233a) and guide bearing (234).
Mount the upper casing wear ring and assemble the first stage cover.

Assemble the lower intermediate case with the first stage on the suction case 
 by tightening the screws and nuts (X5).
Assemble the impeller second stage as followed in the first stage.

Assemble the upper intermediate case with the lower intermediate case by 
 tightening the screws and nuts (X4).
Assemble the discharge case shaft sleeve (233b) and bearing (234).

Assemble the upper intermediate case with the discharge case by tightening the 
 screws and nuts X3

Assemble the intermediate shaft with the lower shaft by tightening the 
 coupling between them.

Assemble the lower column (926) with the discharge case by tightening the 
 screws and nuts (X2).
Mount the shaft sleeve (233c) and bushing (933).

Assemble the intermediate shaft with the upper shaft by tightening the 
 coupling between them.

Assemble the top column (926) with the lower column by tightening the screws 
 and nuts (X1).
Assemble the casted discharge head (952).

Mount the shaft sleeve (233d), packing (11), lantern (225), then mount the 
 gland (241) and mount the water shield (32).

Mount the coupling between the pump shaft and the motor shaft, adjust the 
 alignment and then fix the coupling.
Assemble and fix the motor.
Now the pump is completely assembled.
Open the suction and delivery valves of the pump.

Check the direction of rotation of the pump (by pushing the electric button of 
 the motor instantaneously).

Introduction
This document outlines 
the major maintenance procedures P1, to be performed every five years as 
indicated by Y5 in the title block.
This pump (4 pumps) function to wash 
the traveling water screens from plastics, wood, fungi, and greases.
Technical Specifications
Liquid Pumped | : | Nile River water
Discharge Pressure | : | 5 kg/cm2
Speed | : | 1480 rpm
Power | : | 70 HP
Temperature | : | 30 oC
Full Load Torque | : | 968 Lb.ft
Rated Flow | : | 3833 L / minute
The first draft is initiated by eng. Mohamed Abdel Azeem, tested by eng. Zakria 
Radwan Hassanain, revised by eng. Samir Abdel Gelil: EDEPC 
inspection and quality control general director, accepted by eng. Mohamed Farag 
Anan: general manager, and approved by eng. Mohamed El-Sarrag: head sector of 
Damietta 3x135MW PS.
This document accepted by eng.
 Samir Abdel Gilel: EDEPC 
 inspection and 
 quality control general director & MPIS coordinator, and 
 certified by accountant: Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman EDEPC planning & financial 
 predicting head sector and supervisor of inspection & 
 quality control's head sector.

 staff should carry the suitable safety category.

 is required.
